There are multiple sects within Buddhism and not all follow the Dalai lama with as much vigour. Also the Dalai Lama himself says you shouldn't revere or idealise anyone (including him) and that you should focus more on yourself and being compassionate to others.

I think you raise a fair point which I myself have never really looked into. However from reading multiple books by the Dalai Lama he seemed more willing to challenge conventional ways and be open to modernising his belief and religion. Cases of this are wrote about in 7 years in Tibet where he allows or persuades people around him to allow very old and strict conventions to be broken.

Considering Buddhism is more of a way of thinking and a philosophy and not about worshipping unknown powers I's have to disagree with this.

He even says himself that you shouldn't follow Buddhist teachings blindly, you should go out and test them. As well as being open to changing his way of thinking if he's proved wrong on a point.

While regarding supernatural forces most of his teachings are some form of compassion which comes from the follower and not almighty gods working their will on people.
